report.summary: Prevent silent divergence by combining a single verdict vocabulary (canonical health states) with a consistency test across surfaces. The vocabulary ensures compatibility; the diversity test detects hidden disagreements. Collapsing to one engine removes diversity and risks single-point failures.
risks: Even with a vocabulary, modules may interpret thresholds differently; regular calibration needed.
Consistency tests may cause false positives if modules have different latency/refresh rates.
Diverse modules may have common failure modes if underlying dependencies overlap (e.g., Windows system calls).
todos: Define a canonical health vocabulary (e.g., healthy, degraded, failed, unknown) with optional structured reasons.
Implement multiple independent health assembly modules (e.g., resource monitor, LLM heartbeat, egress fence status).
Add a reconciler module that compares health verdicts and raises an alert on divergence.

handoff.suggestion: Use an open standard like CloudEvents or a custom JSON schema for health reports. The reconciler can be an LLM call that gauges the severity of divergence and logs diagnostic context.

name: q16-divergent-health-surfaces
question: When several modules independently answer the same operational question ('is the system healthy?'), what architectural patterns keep them from silently diverging: a single verdict vocabulary, a consistency test between surfaces, or collapsing to one engine with multiple views?
